annotator: Single agent, visual inspection of each photograph before any OCR was run on this set. No independent adjudication.
protocol: Each photograph was opened and read by eye, and the ingredient text and expected allergen outcome were written down before the evaluation script existed. These are agent-created annotations on an unblinded development set, not externally validated ground truth, and the denominators are far too small to support an accuracy claim. Filenames, Commons descriptions and product knowledge must not supply text that is not legible in the image.
scope: Allergen screening only. No legal, medical or safety verdict is annotated. 'Expected' below is what the deterministic lexicon should return given the FSSAI reg. 5(3) categories it screens against; where the expectation is 'nothing', that is a negative control, and a detection there is a false positive.

lexicon_change_before_this_run.reason: Reading habanero-condiment.jpg by eye showed a cross-contact statement worded 'contains dairy, tree nuts, and eggs'. The lexicon had no entry for the word 'dairy', so it would have missed a milk cross-contact that a human reads immediately.
lexicon_change_before_this_run.found_by: visual inspection of the photograph, before OCR was run on this set
lexicon_change_before_this_run.recorded_because: the term was added before the first evaluation run, so this set never scored the pre-change lexicon; the change is disclosed rather than hidden inside a passing number

images.expected_reason: Out of scope by design, not by failure. The ingredient cue recognises English and Devanagari; a Dutch or Czech block is not read, so nothing should be reported rather than something guessed. Recorded here because a real allergen list going unreported is a limitation worth measuring even when it is intended.
